scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The imported destination covers 1492 to 1500 in the Paraguayan Chaco. Those dates do not establish the origin or disappearance of a living people. No successor is manufactured, and imported geometry is unchanged and unverified.

Angaité is not equated with a single immutable precolonial state. Memorias Angaité and Villagra discuss several related groups, varying names and changing affiliations. No unsupported etymology or pejorative outsider gloss is repeated.

Villagra’s 2014 book distinguishes the Angaité of Puerto Pinasco from the Maskoy of Puerto Casado. Industrial details used here come from the Pinasco discussion, printed pages 259 to 263. Company ownership and closing dates have differing accounts noted in the text; the card avoids a falsely exact single closing year.

The 1910 to 1931 phase is approximate and describes expansion, not first contact everywhere. Colonial accounts quoted inside the book are assessed as attributed documents; their derogatory characterizations are not adopted.
The 2005 recreation period is supported by the introduction, printed page 8, and the first-person fieldwork account, printed page 14. It is not an assertion that these sports existed before contact.

The atlas chapter was downloaded and extracted. Printed page 428 was rendered and visually inspected, confirming that its livelihood data concern La Patria. The introductory PDF at https://www.ine.gov.py/Publicaciones/Biblioteca/Web%20Atlas%20Indigena/Presentacion.pdf identifies the August 2002 census. No present-day demographic estimate is inferred.

The atlas records La Patria as multiethnic, predominantly Angaité. Its crops, occupations and materials are local census observations, not exclusive ethnic traits or universal practices. Housing and language percentages from other pages are not silently assigned to the whole people.

The land article is an advocacy and memory-project account published May 12, 2025. The card attributes its dispute history and testimony. The full judicial order was not inspected; the card does not claim an independently established legal precedent or repeat personal accusations against the named occupier.

The land article places acquisition in 1983 and title in 1995 but also cites legal-personality documentation. The card uses the well-supported 1983 acquisition and does not equate legal personality automatically with a land-title instrument.

The SPL Koahlvo PDF could not be downloaded (HTTP 403). Its contents are described only through the directly read 2023 presentation by Ladislaa Alcaraz; no claim is made to have inspected the full volume or its participant list.

The 2024 youth-workshop report differentiates Qom fiber recording from Angaité plant-name recording. Its July to September date range and September update are preserved; an August post date is not treated as proof that all later workshops had already occurred.

The July 2024 SPL report credits Félix Navarro and Herminia Rivero. No plant recipe, dose or claim of clinical effectiveness is supplied. Audiovisual outputs were not independently watched, and their existence and process are described from project reports.
Independent historical review, identity and chronology assessment, border verification and depth certification remain pending.
